selectionRule: Independent module branches pass review and execution gates before integration. Execution success is not answer correctness; the final dev selection is recorded separately.

events.problem: analysis_protocol_error: ModularRSI analysis must return a list of findings
analysis_protocol_error: finding must cite an editable file and supplied tasks

reviews.reason: The edit does not actually address the cited findings. The deterministic pass is overconfident: for the named failing tasks it always returns a non-None span (usually the candidate's own exact span), so the side-model fallback is never invoked. Concretely it still yields 'ICC Umpire of the Year' instead of 'Umpire of the Year', 'the Chameleon' instead of the full supplied title, 'Holger Hammerich' instead of 'Holger Aagaard Hammerich', the truncated clause, and 'no-kill animal shelter' instead of 'no-kill shelter'. Because full-exact candidate spans receive the highest score, the rule cannot prefer a more complete or more minimal context-supported official form as the finding requires. It adds a large heuristic/side-model pass without fixing the reported failures.

The edit hardcodes a short-answer-only final normalizer into the shared runtime/agent.py without gating on the workspace/task instructions. It always tells the side model the task expects a short canonical answer and always strips Markdown/whitespace, so long-form, formatted, or code answers in other modules would be corrupted. It also runs after _run_before_final_hooks, meaning it can override explicit before_final replace decisions and adds an extra side call rather than reusing the existing gate result. The deterministic fallback is over-aggressive (e.g. 'Answer Man' becomes 'Man' and multi-line answers are collapsed), so the change is not a reusable, interface-preserving harness improvement.

The edit adds a generic-looking final-answer grounding helper, but its logic short-circuits before the side LLM whenever the candidate is already an exact substring of the supplied context. That leaves several listed failures unchanged: 5ac513d0's 'Alpine skiing' occurs in 'Olympic alpine skiing history' and is returned instead of 'alpine ski racer'; 5a834e38's 'Holger Hammerich' occurs as the context title and is returned instead of 'Holger Aagaard Hammerich'; 5a851d48's truncated sentence is a verbatim context substring and is not expanded to the full ground-truth sentence; and 5ab2c508's 'heavily downtuned, mid-paced guitar riffs' is returned instead of the required shorter span 'heavily downtuned, mid-paced'. Thus the normalization step does not actually reconcile over-specific, under-specific, or partial candidates when those candidates already appear in the context, so it fails to address the core findings.

The edit adds a reusable final-answer grounding step to runtime/agent.py for the no-tool-call and forced-answer paths. It parses a supplied Context/Question block generically, detects short-answer prompts, and uses the existing Context.side_text helper followed by deterministic span verification against the context, with raw-candidate fallback when extraction or verification fails. It does not hardcode task IDs or answers, does not change the underlying model, and preserves run()'s signature and Context interfaces.

The edit adds a generic side-model final-answer gate in the no-tool-call branch, reusing existing Context.side_text, remaining_turns, and _final_continue_max. It is fail-open when the side model is unavailable or its decision is unparseable, and it preserves the existing accept/continue flow by appending feedback as a user message. It contains no task IDs or memorized answers and does not modify the underlying main model; it directly addresses the finding that any non-empty output is accepted without verifying completeness/exactness.

The patch adds a generic side-model completion gate in runtime/agent.py's no-tool-call branch, using the existing ctx.side_text path to accept, correct, or continue candidate answers with targeted feedback while respecting remaining_turns and the final-continue budget. It preserves the run and Context interfaces, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and does not change the underlying model configuration.

The normalization is unsafe: it blindly removes the final comma-separated segment, so a correct concise answer such as '2,300' is truncated to '2' (and 'Bishop Grosseteste University has around 2,300 full-time students.' becomes 'Bishop Grosseteste University has around 2'), directly corrupting one of the target short-answer tasks. It also fails to detect sentence-like candidates such as 'Jazzy B was a Punjabi language Bhangra singer-songwriter.' because the sentence detector uses only a small fixed prefix list and rejects only >10-word text, so that candidate would be accepted as concise instead of triggering a revision to the bare short answer. Thus it does not preserve already-concise answers or fully address the findings.

The normalization and side-LLM gate are generic and target the right short-answer gap, but the gate is run unconditionally after _run_before_final_hooks even when a workspace before_final middleware already validated or replaced the answer. That does not preserve the existing before_final interface: it adds extra side-LLM calls and can override an explicit middleware accept/replace, which would also break the existing middleware side-call test. It should be scoped to run only when no workspace before_final hook exists, and the side-unavailable fallback should preserve the original candidate rather than returning the normalized form.

The patch adds a reusable, generic final-answer normalization/grounding gate in the no-tool-call completion path. It contains no task IDs or memorized answers, does not modify the main model configuration, and preserves existing function signatures and the before-final hook flow. It directly addresses the reported deficiency by stripping padding and using one existing side-LLM call to extract the exact supported answer span from supplied context, with a safe padding-only fallback.

The no-answer/refusal detector is incomplete: phrases observed in the supplied failures such as 'Not specified in the context.' and 'Not mentioned in the provided context.' are classified as usable answers, so the re-extract fallback never triggers and a side-model refusal can be returned as the final answer. In addition, _is_exact_short_span skips normalization for punctuation-only single-token candidates but returns the original punctuated text, so format-only errors can still pass through. The edit therefore does not reliably address the findings.

The edit adds reusable, generic final-answer gating, context-span grounding, and completion-check helpers in runtime/agent.py, all using the existing ctx.side_text path. It preserves run/Context interfaces, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and does not change the underlying model. The no-tool-call path and forced-answer path are both covered as described in the findings.

The edit is a generic, reusable harness improvement in runtime/agent.py: it consolidates the redundant final-answer gate/grounding/completion-check paths into one internal helper, tightens context-span matching with word boundaries to avoid partial matches such as China in Indochina, and strengthens the extraction prompt to preserve exact context wording. It only touches internal final-answer helpers and call sites, preserving public interfaces, and does not introduce task IDs, memorized answers, unrelated edits, or model changes. Findings are empty, so there are no unaddressed issues.

The change is a generic improvement to the final-answer gate in runtime/agent.py: it adds reusable yes/no and explicit short-answer instruction detection, makes the completion detector authoritative before deterministic grounding, and restricts grounding to spans that are safe to normalize. It preserves the existing function signatures/return contract and introduces no task IDs, memorized answers, model changes, or unrelated edits.

The edit is a reusable harness improvement in runtime/agent.py: it reorders final-answer padding cleanup to handle bold labels and numeric answers like 1971. without misclassifying them as list markers, broadens context-header detection, refines short-answer detection so open-ended why/how stays long-form while how many/much/old questions still trigger, and grounds single-token extracted answers against the supplied context. It preserves existing function signatures and return contracts, only touches internal helpers, and contains no task IDs, memorized answers, unrelated edits, or underlying-model changes.

The edit is a generic harness improvement: it moves final-continue budget enforcement out of the completion-check helper into the final-answer loop after deterministic grounding, preserves the (action, candidate, feedback) return contract, and accepts verified grounded spans on the last turn instead of needlessly continuing or dropping the answer. No task-specific data, task IDs, answer memorization, unrelated model changes, or interface breaks are introduced.

events.problem: analysis_protocol_error: finding must cite an editable file and supplied tasks

reviews.reason: The edit is a generic, reusable Stop-hook improvement that enforces the existing short-answer output contract by blocking trailing parentheticals, dash/semicolon elaborations, and bare Yes/No plus extra clauses on the first Stop. It preserves decide(event) and the CLI, returns {} when stop_hook_active is true so the agent can still exit, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and directly addresses the contrastive over-answer failures without modifying the model.

The change adds reusable, task-agnostic heuristics to the completion_check Stop hook for the two missing short-answer over-answer patterns (locative preposition + capitalized token and cardinal + lowercase token). It preserves decide()'s interface and the stop_hook_active exit path, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and matches the requested finding.

The patch is a reusable, task-agnostic completion_check improvement: it strips Markdown emphasis and terminal sentence punctuation before applying the existing short-answer heuristics, and refactors those heuristics into _has_over_answer without changing decide()'s interface or the stop_hook_active early-return path. It contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and the patched file compiles and behaves correctly on the relevant raw/decorated cases.

The patch is a reusable, task-agnostic completion_check improvement: it adds top-level comma and trailing to-infinitive elaboration detection on the already-normalized Stop message, with generic exemptions for dates, thousands separators, numeric ranges, and inverted names. It preserves the decide() interface and stop_hook_active early-exit path, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and compiles successfully.

The edit adds generic, reusable answer-extraction and output-contract rules to the SearchQA skill that directly address the noted failure modes: exact surface-form matching, no extra qualifiers or formatting, and handling near-synonym/related unit labels. It contains no task IDs, memorized answers, or task-specific logic, does not alter model internals or interfaces, and is appropriate as a harness-level skill improvement.

The edit is a reusable, task-agnostic improvement to the SearchQA skill. It directly addresses both findings by adding a pre-extraction step that identifies the requested slot and cardinality and by strengthening the extraction/output rules to preserve exact minimal spans, leading prepositions/articles, full names, and official wording while avoiding incidental prepositions or slot substitution. It contains no task IDs, memorized answers, or model changes and preserves the existing interface.

The edit is a reusable, general documentation change to the SearchQA output contract. It does not include task IDs or memorized answers, preserves the skill interface, and directly addresses the finding by requiring the shortest contiguous slot-filling phrase, with a generic class-word example rather than a task-specific solution.

The edit adds a generic PostToolUse hook for the Skill tool that reinforces the answer-format contract whenever the Skill tool loads. It preserves the decide(event) interface by still returning {} for all other events, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and does not modify the underlying model. This directly addresses the finding that the existing identity hook misses the post-tool opportunity to restate the output contract.

The edit only expands the PostToolUse Skill hook's additionalContext with generic answer-format rules for yes/no verification, category/style/type labels, number/ordinal surface forms, and named entities. It preserves the decide(event) return contract and still returns {} for all other events, contains no task IDs or memorized answers, and does not modify the underlying model. It directly addresses the reported non-canonical short-answer failures.

The edit extends the existing PostToolUse/Skill additionalContext with generic, reusable instructions that match both findings: it directs Who questions to return the defining descriptive predicate rather than an alternative name, field/industry questions to return the abstract field label, where questions to return only the place-name phrase, and measurement questions to return the requested dimension's exact numeric phrase and unit. It contains no task IDs, memorized answers, or model changes, and it preserves the hook interface by only modifying the prompt string content.

The edit keeps the hook interface and event gating intact and only replaces the additionalContext prompt. It is worded generically (no task IDs or memorized answers) and directly addresses both reported surface-form failures: preserving full place phrases with trailing location qualifiers and copying exact noun phrases for sport/type/description questions instead of paraphrasing. This is a reusable harness-level guidance improvement, not a task-specific solution or model change.

The completion_check.py edit introduces an over-broad, brittle comma-elaboration heuristic that conflicts with the other edits and the findings. For example, it blocks 'John F. Kennedy International Airport, New York', the exact full place phrase the new tool_interaction hook instructs the model to preserve, and other valid comma-bearing short answers such as 'New York, New York'. It also fails to incorporate several tool_interaction findings (yes/no verification and semantic-type slot guidance). This creates regressions and is not a safe reusable harness improvement.

The edit is a reusable, task-agnostic harness improvement: completion_check.py adds generic short-answer enforcement heuristics, tool_interaction.py injects a matching output-contract reminder only on PostToolUse for the Skill tool, and SKILL.md documents the same exact/minimal extraction contract. It preserves the decide(event) hook interfaces and expected return shapes, including permissive re-entry when stop_hook_active is true, and contains no task IDs, memorized answers, model changes, or unrelated edits. The tool_interaction wording is aligned with the completion hook and skill, avoiding the prior conflict over trailing comma-separated qualifiers.

The completion_check.py edit removes the generic inverted-name exemption, so _has_comma_elaboration now blocks legitimate comma-bearing short answers such as 'Smith, John' or 'Winesburg, Ohio'; this is a behavior regression rather than a reusable harness improvement. The tool_interaction.py edit swaps the broader SearchQA output-contract guidance for narrow special-case rules about yes/no and 'Who is/was [name]?' questions, which is task-specific prompt tailoring, and neither edit addresses any reported finding.

The edit is a reusable harness-level improvement: completion_check adds a structural comma exemption for multi-part proper-noun phrases and generational suffixes without hard-coding task IDs or answers; tool_interaction adds a defensive non-dict no-op guard and clarifies the searchqa output contract for yes/no and location/base slots; SKILL.md is updated consistently. Existing decide() return interfaces are preserved, no underlying model is changed, and the empty findings list leaves nothing unaddressed.

The edit is a reusable, task-agnostic harness improvement: completion_check.py replaces the brittle token-count exemption with a generic administrative-division suffix check, so full location/name phrases such as Los Angeles, California are preserved while administrative over-answers such as Dawson County, Montana remain blocked; tool_interaction.py and SKILL.md are aligned on exact-context-phrase extraction and retain the same decide() hook interfaces and JSON return shapes. It contains no task IDs, memorized answers, underlying-model changes, or unrelated edits.
